QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_30

question.text: Institutional LPs often pursue an 'over-commitment strategy'. What does this mean in the AIF context (Section 7.1.1)?

answer.text: LPs commit more than 100% of their net worth to a single AIF.
The fund over-commits to a single investee, breaching the 25% cap.
The GP oversubscribes the fund beyond the SEBI-registered corpus ceiling.
Forecasted capital calls on outstanding commitments to multiple AIFs exceed the LP's current cash balances, relying on interim distributions from older vintages to meet new calls.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.1.1(4) Cash Management: 'Institutional investors often pursue an over-commitment strategy in which forecasted capital calls on outstanding commitments exceed current cash balances.' The bet is that distributions from mature funds finance calls of newer funds, minimising idle-cash drag. The Trap: A is a risk-management breach, not over-commitment. C is a SEBI regulatory breach (green-shoe only 25%). D is a concentration breach. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-A test LP cash-management strategies. Pension-fund LPs (CalPERS, CPPIB) publish over-commitment ratios of 110-130%. Manager's Pro-Tip: As a Cat I/II Manager, help LPs model their over-commitment by publishing a capital-call and distribution-pace chart in the annual LP meeting — LPs with liquidity profiling can commit bigger tickets and re-up faster.
